s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial pain with cranial nerve involvement and skull base abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive right mandibular pain radiating to the zygomatic and mastoid regions
Enlargement of the right sphenoid sinus with bone thickening and sclerosis
Soft tissue protruding through a breach in the lateral recess wall of the sphenoid sinus
key_facts: 83-year-old man presented with 6 months of progressive right mandibular pain
Pain radiates to the zygomatic and mastoid regions
Requires oxycodone, paracetamol, and ketorolac for relief
Empirical course of prednisone provided no benefit
Contrast-enhanced maxillofacial CT showed enlargement of the right sphenoid sinus
Gadolinium-enhanced MRI demonstrated soft tissue protruding through a breach in the lateral recess wall
Intracranial extension into the cavernous sinus surrounded the Gasserian ganglion
T2-weighted images showed a markedly hypointense signal in the lateral recess
Endoscopic evaluation revealed purulent discharge in the sphenoethmoidal recess
Histopathology was negative for hyphae and neoplastic cells
Cultures grew no bacteria or fungi
Follow-up MRI confirmed persistent inflammation of the sphenoid sinus, skull base, and pterygoid fossa

shortlist.label: Sphenoid sinus pyocele
shortlist.why_kept: Purulent discharge in the sphenoethmoidal recess and pyocele found during endoscopic sinus surgery

shortlist.label: Sphenoid sinus mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: Enlargement of the right sphenoid sinus and soft tissue protruding through a breach in the lateral recess wall

shortlist.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive facial pain with cranial nerve involvement and skull base abnormalities

shortlist.label: Trigeminal schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Intracranial extension into the cavernous sinus surrounded the Gasserian ganglion

shortlist.label: Sphenoid sinus carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Persistent inflammation of the sphenoid sinus, skull base, and pterygoid fossa despite negative histopathology and cultures

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with purulent discharge in the sphenoethmoidal recess, soft tissue protruding through a breach in the lateral recess wall, and the finding of a pyocele obstructing the sphenoid ostium during endoscopic evaluation support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Sphenoid sinus mucocele
rejected.why: While mucoceles can cause similar symptoms, the presence of purulent discharge and a pyocele suggests an infectious process

rejected.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with painful ophthalmoplegia, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Trigeminal schwannoma
rejected.why: The absence of neoplastic cells on histopathology makes this diagnosis unlikely

rejected.label: Sphenoid sinus carcinoma
rejected.why: The negative histopathology for neoplastic cells rules out this diagnosis
